subject: CatalystPay DPA — initial redline & counsel questions
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@catalystpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CatalystPay DPA — initial redline & counsel questions

Hi Emma,

Thanks for sending over CatalystPay's DPA. Please find attached our first-pass redline (CatalystPay_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf). I wanted to highlight the items we've flagged as higher priority for discussion so we can focus the call:

- Subprocessors: We've added language to require 30 days' advance notice for material changes and an objection/cure process.
- Cross-border transfers: we proposed the EU Addendum + SCCs fallback; we asked for clarity on any in-country hosting obligations.
- Breach notifications: we proposed 72 hours for notification to align with our operational model (we flagged CatalystPay's 24-hour requirement).
- Audit/SOC evidence: we can provide our most recent SOC 2 report under NDA; requested scope clarification for onsite audits.
- Retention and deletion: we suggested a 90-day deletion window after termination for customer data (exceptions for backup retention).

Attached: CatalystPay_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (redline), plus a short annotated summary in Redwood_DPA_Response_round1.docx.

Would your team be available this week for a 30–45m call to go through the redline? If we can align on the high-level points above we can prepare a DocuSign route for round 1 execution.

Next steps from our side if helpful: we will prepare a one-page mapping of CatalystPay clauses -> Redwood proposed language and indicate which items require legal escalation.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: CatalystPay Legal <privacy-counsel@catalystpay.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Kelly <emma.kelly@catalystpay.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CatalystPay DPA — initial redline & counsel questions

Thanks Lauren — we reviewed the redline. Please find our annotated version attached (CatalystPay_DPA_annotated_by_Counsel.pdf). A few quick points from counsel that will help us prepare for the call:

1) Subprocessors: CatalystPay requires a 30-day notice but expects that minimal operational updates (e.g., switching a monitoring vendor) do not trigger objections. Please confirm Redwood's objection scope.

2) Breach timeline: We have a 24-hour notification requirement in our standard DPA for critical incidents. We understand operational constraints — can you split the notification into (a) initial notification within 24 hours with high-level details and (b) a fuller incident report within 72 hours?

3) Data transfers: We prefer contractually binding SCCs + a transfer addendum. If Redwood intends to rely on standard contractual clauses only for certain modules, please specify which ones.

4) Audit rights: We are asking for a standard audit right for a third-party assessor once annually. Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a mutually agreed assessor and a process to scope the review to data-processing controls only.

5) SOC 2: Counsel would like to review Redwood's latest SOC 2 Type II (2026) under an NDA. Please share the link and NDA process.

We used comments in the attached PDF rather than inline redlines where we had policy constraints. Can we schedule a call Thursday 14 Apr at 10:00 PT?

Regards,
CatalystPay Legal (on behalf of Emma Kelly)
privacy-counsel@catalystpay.com
[Attachment: CatalystPay_DPA_annotated_by_Counsel.pdf (pdf)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: CatalystPay DPA — annotated counsel comments

Forwarding CatalystPay's annotated comments and my quick reading. Key suggested positions below — these are draft and we should confirm with privacy lead if anything escalates to exceptions: 

> On breach notification (24h vs 72h): propose compromise — commit to an initial alert within 24 hours for incidents meeting our "critical" definition (data exfiltration/production-impacting incidents), and a fuller report within 72 hours. We'll document the "critical" criteria in the DPA schedule to avoid ambiguity.

> Subprocessors: accept 30-day notice but narrow objection right to (a) new subprocessors that will have access to customer content, and (b) changes to subprocessors processing special categories. That preserves operational flexibility.

> SCCs & Transfers: agree to SCCs + addendum; however, call out that certain metrics/observability modules that run in customer-resident regions (if requested) may be covered by local hosting commitments — we'll confirm per-account.

> Audit rights: agree to annual third-party assessment with mutual agreement on scope, but push to provide SOC 2 report in lieu of full onsite audit for standard customers; escalate if CatalystPay insists on onsite.

> SOC 2: Provide link to SOC 2 (redwood.share link) after their NDA — include a short checklist of what the SOC covers so counsel knows scope.

I drafted short answers in Redwood_DPA_Response_round1.docx (attached to Lauren's original). If helpful, Neha, can you own the call coordination and propose times? We should keep legal (privacy) and account exec on the call.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Hi Emma / CatalystPay team,

Thanks for the detailed annotations — very helpful. After internal review (Monica & privacy team), here is what we can confirm for round 1: 

1) Breach notifications: Redwood will provide an initial notification within 24 hours for incidents meeting our defined "critical incident" threshold and deliver a full incident report within 72 hours. We'll include the critical incident definition in the DPA schedule to make this operational.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood accepts 30-day notice. Objection rights will be limited to subprocessors that (i) will have access to customer content and (ii) process special categories of data. For all other changes we will provide notice only.

3) Transfers: Redwood will sign SCCs + a transfer addendum. If CatalystPay requires in-country hosting for particular modules, please identify which modules and we'll scope options (regional hosting / dedicated pools) separately.

4) Audit / SOC 2: We can provide our SOC 2 Type II (2026) under NDA. For most customers, we will provide the SOC 2 and support a scoped third-party assessment; onsite audits are reserved for enterprise customers with contractual commitments due to the operational impact.

5) Retention: We confirm a 90-day deletion window post-termination for customer content, with standard backup retention exceptions.

Next steps: 
- Please review the attached Redwood_DPA_Response_round1.docx for clause-by-clause proposed language.
- If CatalystPay is comfortable with the above, we can route the DPA through DocuSign for round 1 signature; link below.
- Proposed DocuSign route (round 1): Redwood (Laurence, legal) -> CatalystPay legal -> CatalystPay exec. Sign-off timeline suggested: 72 hours for review + 5 business days for exec review.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/some-fake-sign-link/CAT-3389
SOC 2 (NDA required): https://redwood.share/controls/soc2-report-2026

Would Thursday at 10:00 PT still work for a call? If so, Neha will send a calendar invite with a short agenda (breach cadence, subprocessor scope, transfer mechanism).

Thanks — looking forward to aligning and getting round 1 executed.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
